mukattaa-card.heading: 14 letters, the signature of 29 suras
mukattaa-card.body: LINGUISTIC DNA 14 letters, the signature of 29 suras الٓمٓ · ذٰلِكَ الْكِتَابُ لَا رَيْبَ فِيهِ “Alif-Lām-Mīm. That is the Book; no doubt in it...” — AL-BAQARA 2:1-2 14 letters open 29 suras, 25% of the Quran. They fall into 4 major families (Alif-Lām-Mīm, Alif-Lām-Rā, Ḥawāmīm, Ṭā-Sīn), each with its own linguistic signature. Their meaning has been debated for 1,400 years; their pattern is mathematically consistent. EXAMINE THE 14 LETTERS AND 4 FAMILIES → 14 letters · 29 suras · 4 families

ritim-card.heading: Neither poetry nor prose
ritim-card.body: IMPOSSIBLE RHYTHM Neither poetry nor prose وَالنَّجْمِ اِذَا هَوٰى “By the star when it falls...” — AN-NAJM 53:1 In 7th-century Arabia, speech was either poetry bound to one of 16 meters or free prose. The Quran fits neither: it has rhythm but no meter. The classical rhetorical tradition treats this form as a category of its own within iʿjāz al-bayān. SEE THE RHYTHM ANALYSIS → 16 meters · examples from an-Najm, al-Kawthar, ad-Ḍuḥā

arabic: لَقَدْ اَرْسَلْنَا رُسُلَنَا بِالْبَيِّنَاتِ وَاَنْزَلْنَا مَعَهُمُ الْكِتَابَ وَالْمِيزَانَ لِيَقُومَ النَّاسُ بِالْقِسْطِ وَاَنْزَلْنَا الْحَدِيدَ فِيهِ بَأْسٌ شَدِيدٌ وَمَنَافِعُ لِلنَّاسِ وَلِيَعْلَمَ اللّٰهُ مَنْ يَنْصُرُهُ وَرُسُلَهُ بِالْغَيْبِ اِنَّ اللّٰهَ قَوِيٌّ عَزِيزٌ

ثُمَّ خَلَقْنَا النُّطْفَةَ عَلَقَةً فَخَلَقْنَا الْعَلَقَةَ مُضْغَةً فَخَلَقْنَا الْمُضْغَةَ عِظَاماً فَكَسَوْنَا الْعِظَامَ لَحْماً ثُمَّ اَنْشَأْنَاهُ خَلْقاً اٰخَرَ فَتَبَارَكَ اللّٰهُ اَحْسَنُ الْخَالِقِينَ
bilimsel-card.heading: The Quran informs; the rest is reflection
bilimsel-card.body: SCIENTIFIC SIGNS The Quran informs; the rest is reflection Iron (Ḥadīd 57:25; 1957), the expansion of the universe (Ẓāriyāt 51:47; Hubble 1929), the barrier between two seas (ar-Raḥmān 55:19-20; oceanography), embryology (al-Muʾminūn 23:14). This page makes no "scientific miracle" claim; for each verse it sets classical tafsir, the modern parallel and a critical note side by side. Hubble · 1929 Cosmic expansion وَالسَّمَاءَ بَنَيْنَاهَا بِاَيْدٍ وَاِنَّا لَمُوسِعُونَ aẓ-Ẓāriyāt 51:47 Astrophysics · 1957 The origin of iron لَقَدْ اَرْسَلْنَا رُسُلَنَا بِالْبَيِّنَاتِ وَاَنْزَلْنَا مَعَهُمُ الْكِتَابَ وَالْمِيزَانَ لِيَقُومَ النَّاسُ بِالْقِسْطِ وَاَنْزَلْنَا الْحَدِيدَ فِيهِ بَأْسٌ شَدِيدٌ وَمَنَافِعُ لِلنَّاسِ وَلِيَعْلَمَ اللّٰهُ مَنْ يَنْصُرُهُ وَرُسُلَهُ بِالْغَيْبِ اِنَّ اللّٰهَ قَوِيٌّ عَزِيزٌ al-Ḥadīd 57:25 Oceanography · 1960s The barrier between two seas مَرَجَ الْبَحْرَيْنِ يَلْتَقِيَانِ ar-Raḥmān 55:19 Embryology · 20th c. Clinging clot → lump → bone ثُمَّ خَلَقْنَا النُّطْفَةَ عَلَقَةً فَخَلَقْنَا الْعَلَقَةَ مُضْغَةً فَخَلَقْنَا الْمُضْغَةَ عِظَاماً فَكَسَوْنَا الْعِظَامَ لَحْماً ثُمَّ اَنْشَأْنَاهُ خَلْقاً اٰخَرَ فَتَبَارَكَ اللّٰهُ اَحْسَنُ الْخَالِقِينَ al-Muʾminūn 23:14 READ THE FOUR VERSES AND THEIR NOTES → 4 verses · classical + modern

tarih-card.heading: Three claims, three historical traces
tarih-card.body: 10 HISTORICAL TRACES Three claims, three historical traces فَالْيَوْمَ نُنَجِّيكَ بِبَدَنِكَ “This day We shall preserve your body, that you may be a sign to those after you.” YŪNUS 10:92 Yūnus 10:92 says Pharaoh's body will be preserved as a sign; the royal mummies became more visible in modern literature after the 1881 Deir el-Bahari excavation led by Maspero's team. Hāmān is mentioned in the Quran as one of Pharaoh's circle. Ar-Rūm 30:2-4 foretells a Byzantine victory after their defeat, and it came within a few years. Examine the three traces →

arabic: اِنَّا نَحْنُ نَزَّلْنَا الذِّكْرَ وَاِنَّا لَهُ لَحَافِظُونَ
koruma-card.heading: 1,400 years, one text
koruma-card.body: 15 LIVING PRESERVATION 1,400 years, one text اِنَّا نَحْنُ نَزَّلْنَا الذِّكْرَ وَاِنَّا لَهُ لَحَافِظُونَ “Indeed, We sent down the Reminder, and We shall preserve it.” AL-ḤIJR 15:9 The Birmingham manuscript (2015, carbon-14: 568-645) is the oldest fragment that overlaps with the Prophet's lifetime. Today millions of ḥuffāẓ carry the whole Quran by heart, and the text read in Mecca, Istanbul and Jakarta is the same. The isnād chain documents that oral transmission. What stays fixed is the consonantal skeleton (rasm); the mutawātir qirāʾāt differences leave that skeleton intact and stand beside it as a separate, documented layer. Follow the preservation chain →

arabic: وَاِذَا سَاَلَكَ عِبَادِي عَنِّي فَاِنِّي قَرِيبٌ
dua-card.heading: A direct dialogue between servant and Lord
dua-card.body: LANGUAGE OF PRAYER A direct dialogue between servant and Lord وَاِذَا سَاَلَكَ عِبَادِي عَنِّي فَاِنِّي قَرِيبٌ “When My servants ask about Me, I am near; I respond to the call of the caller.” — AL-BAQARA 2:186 Prayer in the Quran does not fit a single literary formula; it spreads across several grammatical templates: "iyyāka naʿbudu" in al-Fātiḥa (You alone we worship), the command "Call upon Me" in al-Muʾmin 40:60, the promise "I respond" in al-Baqara 2:186. Supplication takes shape inside these templates. SEE THE PATTERNS OF PRAYER → 10 thematic duʿās · 1 shared grammatical structure

allah-kendini-tanitir.heading: You've seen the creation. Now meet the Creator.
allah-kendini-tanitir.body: CREATION → CREATOR You've seen the creation. Now meet the Creator. وَلِلّٰهِ الْاَسْمَٓاءُ الْحُسْنٰى فَادْعُوهُ بِهَا “To Allah belong the best names, so invoke Him by them.” — A'RĀF 7:180 God describes Himself in the Quran through 114 names and attributes, sometimes in the third person and sometimes directly in the first. Might (Jalāl) and mercy (Jamāl) are held together, in balance. اللَّه Allāh 2,699 occurrences الرَّحْمَٰن ar-Raḥmān 60 occurrences الْعَلِيم al-ʿAlīm 161 occurrences الْحَكِيم al-Ḥakīm 97 occurrences OPEN THE BEAUTIFUL NAMES → 114 names & attributes · 19 thematic axes
